Up at the dusky-blue cottage door, the Wife waves him off with a big smile, the three children crowding round her skirts. Far below, the roofs of the little town lie in the valley. Crisp, sunny morning with long blue shadows.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- Gudbrand: A short, round, easy-going old farmer of about seventy with a round belly, a shiny bald head, fluffy white side-whiskers from his ears down to his jaw, a clean-shaven chin, a big pink nose, small merry blue eyes and a calm, contented smile. He wears a soft dark-green felt hat with a narrow brim, a thick knitted jacket with a black-and-white snowflake pattern and pewter clasps, a red knitted scarf, brown breeches, grey wool stockings and heavy boots, and always has a short curved wooden pipe.
- the Wife: A plump, cheerful farm wife of about sixty-five, a little shorter than Gudbrand, with a round, beaming face, rosy cheeks, a broad, freckled nose, merry hazel eyes that crinkle when she laughs, and grey hair pinned up in a neat bun. She wears a long rose-red wool dress with a white linen collar and rolled-up sleeves, a bright cornflower-blue apron with a big bow at the back, and a cream knitted shawl round her shoulders.

Setting:
- the Hillside Farm: A tiny farm high on a steep, snowy hillside: a low, dark-brown log cottage with a thick, snow-covered turf roof, a stone chimney, two small four-paned windows and a sturdy plank door painted dusky blue, with a little cowshed beside it. A birch and a rowan tree with red berries stand in the yard next to a sheaf of oats on a tall pole, and a narrow path zigzags steeply down towards the valley far below.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago, in a deep mountain valley in the week before Christmas. Gudbrand's small farm sits high up on a steep hillside: a low log cottage and a little cowshed. A narrow path zigzags down past the Neighbour's farm to a small market town by a frozen river, along a snowy road lined with birches and sheaves of oats on poles. Gudbrand and his wife have three small children: a boy of about eight with short black hair and a green jumper, a girl of about six with two stubby fair plaits and a red dress, and a chubby toddler in a long white shirt. The animals: a black cow with a white face, a sandy-yellow fjord horse with a striped pale mane, a fat pink pig, a white nanny goat, a woolly white sheep, a big white goose and a cinnamon-brown rooster.

Then a clear, deep-indigo night full of stars, with every small window glowing candle-yellow. Inside the cottage: warm firelight, straw ornaments and red-and-white cloths. Accents: the Wife's cornflower-blue apron and bright red rowan berries.

places.name: the Cottage Room
places.look: A snug, low-ceilinged log room with honey-brown timber walls. In one corner a whitewashed stone fireplace holds a crackling fire and a black iron pot. illustrations.anchor: Kona hans var den blideste i hele bygda.
illustrations.caption: Brente Gudbrand grøten, sa kona: «Mmm! Røkt grøt!»
illustrations.alt: Gudbrand holder fram en svart gryte med brent grøt som ryker. Kona bøyer seg over gryta med lukkede øyne og smiler, som om det luktet deilig.
illustrations.prompt: Morning in the Cottage Room. By the fireplace, Gudbrand holds up the black iron pot with both hands, and a thin curl of grey smoke rises from the burnt porridge inside; he looks sheepish and apologetic. The Wife leans over the pot with her eyes closed and a blissful smile, sniffing the smoke as if it were the finest dish in the world, a wooden spoon raised in one hand. Pale winter light comes through the frosty window.
